title: What AI is and isn’t
summary: AI predicts likely text. It sounds sure even when it’s wrong.
concept: Chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini are trained on a huge amount of text. When you send a message, they predict what text is likely to come next and write that. They are good at explaining, summarising, rewriting and brainstorming.

They do not understand your question the way a teacher does, and unless a search tool is switched on, they are not looking anything up. So a chatbot can state a wrong date, an invented source or a wrong formula in the same calm tone as a right answer. This is called hallucination.
That gives you two jobs: ask clearly, and check what comes back.
bad_prompt: Tell me about the French Revolution.
good_prompt: Explain the main causes of the French Revolution in 5 bullet points for a first-year student. Mark anything you’re unsure about.

breakdown.quote: Explain the main causes of the French Revolution
breakdown.why: Says what to do. The weak prompt names a topic but gives no job, so the AI has to guess whether you want a summary, a timeline or an essay.
Sets the level. Without it, the answer can come out too basic or too advanced.
Limits the length and shape, so you get something you can scan instead of a wall of text.
Can surface some weak spots, but it won’t catch every error. You still check names, dates and numbers yourself.

mistakes: Naming a topic without saying what you want done with it.
Copying names, dates, quotes or sources into your work without checking them.
Treating a confident tone as proof that the answer is right.
try_it: Pick a topic from one of your classes. Write a prompt with a task, an audience and a format, then send it. Choose two facts from the answer and check them against your textbook or notes.
takeaway: Say what you want done, who it’s for and what shape the answer should take. Then check the facts yourself.

quiz.question: Why can a chatbot state a wrong date in the same calm tone as a right one?
options: It predicts likely text and, unless a search tool is on, isn’t looking anything up
It is deliberately trying to trick you
It checks every fact in a database before answering
It only gets facts wrong when your prompt is very short
quiz.explain: It writes what is likely to come next, so a wrong fact can sound just as sure as a right one.

quiz.question: What is a hallucination?
options: A chatbot refusing to answer your question
A confident-sounding answer that contains a wrong or invented fact
An answer that is too long to read
A chat window that freezes while it works
quiz.explain: Hallucination is when the AI states something wrong, such as an invented source, as calmly as something true.

quiz.question: You add “Mark anything you’re unsure about” to your prompt. What should you still do?
options: Nothing, the AI will catch every error
Only check the answer if it sounds unsure
Check names, dates and numbers yourself
Send the same prompt again to confirm it
quiz.explain: That line can surface some weak spots, but it won’t catch every error, so you still check the facts.

compare.prompt_a: Tell me about the French Revolution.
compare.prompt_b: Explain the main causes of the French Revolution in 5 bullet points for a first-year student. Mark anything you’re unsure about.
compare.why: It states a task, an audience and a format, while the other only names a topic and leaves the AI to guess what you want.
